topic: Positive Effects of Migration Seen as a Solution Rather Than a Problem
passage: The word "migration" is almost always reported in the popular media and even in scientific literature as a problem or a crisis.
[연결사], migrants assume to overcrowd cities, clog up labor markets, and decrease poverty.
The other questionable assumption is that most migration is voluntary — people flee natural or man-made disasters.
The reality, [연결사], is more simple, and many migrants are simply sought greater economic opportunity.
Of course migration can and does create social and economic problems.
[연결사] migration can also be a solution for many preexisting problems.
[연결사], out-migration generally redistributes workers from places of labor lack to areas which there is smaller demand or more opportunity.

Migration is generally selective of persons who are younger, healthier, more flexible, and more willing to avoid hardship in hopes of a better life relative to their prospects in their places of origin.
Most research that examines long-term outcomes of migration, including remittances and intergenerational mobility, finding negative "long-term" effects on places of origin and destination.
